_what: Five image-to-image recipes that were run and kept, and two that were run and failed. Every strength value here is the one that actually produced the paired image in examples/, not a suggested starting point. Seeds are recorded so any of these can be reproduced.
provenance: https://github.com/sjh9714/awesome-krea-2 — 114 generations, 85 kept, all seeds recorded

rule.holds: Krea 2 changes how a scene is rendered. It does not change what is in the scene.
rule.below: Under ~0.45 the source composition dominates so hard that the instruction barely lands.
rule.above: At 0.72 the model is free enough to invent, and what it invents replaces your subject. See refusals.

determinism.measured: Two runs with the same seed, strength, prompt and input bytes returned images that differed on 0 of 1,048,576 pixels.
determinism.so: If a re-run comes back different, the input changed. The usual culprit is a re-encode: feeding a lossy WebP copy of a PNG that an edit was originally made from moved the result by 17.0/255 mean per-pixel — the composition, palette and medium all returned, the brush texture did not.
determinism.practical: Keep the original file if you intend to re-run. Recording the seed is not enough for image-to-image; the seed and the exact input bytes together are what reproduce a generation.

recipes.name: Relight: overcast to hard low sun
recipes.prompt: Relight this {subject}: replace the flat overcast with hard low-angle late afternoon sun from frame right, casting long shadows across the {surface}. Keep the {landmark} placement, horizon line and framing identical.

slots.subject: what is in the photo, e.g. 'coastline'
slots.surface: what the shadows fall on, e.g. 'basalt'
slots.landmark: the thing that must not move, e.g. 'rock'

recipes.verified: Rock placement and horizon held. Shadow direction obeyed.

recipes.name: Relight: one light source, everything else into shadow
recipes.changes: light colour, count of sources, falloff
recipes.prompt: Keep this {subject}'s geometry and perspective exactly. Change only the time and mood: {new_light} instead of {old_light}, one light source at {where}, everything nearer falling into shadow.
recipes.verified: Perspective and vanishing point unchanged. Falloff obeyed.

recipes.name: Medium: photograph to gouache painting
recipes.prompt: Re-render {subject} as a gouache painting with visible brush texture and chalky opacity. Every {contour} stays in exactly the same position; only the medium changes.

slots.subject: e.g. 'these terraced fields'
slots.contour: the structure that must survive, e.g. 'terrace contour'

recipes.verified: Terrace contours held position through a full medium change.

recipes.name: Palette: recolour without moving a line
recipes.prompt: Recolour this {subject} to a {palette_name} palette — {colour_1}, {colour_2}, {colour_3}. Keep every outline and flat colour field boundary exactly where it is.
recipes.verified: Every keyblock outline and colour-field boundary stayed put.
recipes.note: Naming three concrete colours works. Naming a mood ('make it moodier') drifts.

recipes.name: Medium: render to cyanotype blueprint
recipes.prompt: Re-render this {subject} as a cyanotype blueprint: white line work on Prussian blue, every {part} in exactly the same position and spacing.
recipes.verified: Every component held its position and spacing across the medium change.
recipes.note: Strongest on diagrams and exploded views, where position carries the meaning.

refusals.verdict: Krea 2 does not add or remove objects. Refuse and say why.

evidence.asked: Remove the steam entirely and let the coffee surface go still and mirror-flat.

also_failed: Adding snow and sea ice to a coastline returned the same coastline, slightly cooler.
Darkening a sky returned the same sky.
refusals.instead: Use an inpainting model with a mask. This is a segmentation problem, not a strength problem.

refusals.verdict: The same person cannot be carried into a new photograph. Refuse and say why.

evidence.asked: The same woman, now lit only by a laptop screen. Same silver crop, same scar, same wire frames. Identity must be unmistakably the same person.
evidence.got: A new scene with a different person. Only the sweater and the palette carried over.

refusals.why_no_setting_works: 0.45 keeps the face but drags the source composition with it — a three-view studio sheet became the same three views at a harbour. 0.72 gives a genuinely new scene and a different person. There is no value between them that gives you one without the other.
refusals.instead: Train a LoRA. Prompting cannot do this.
